mainTopic: How a baby forms and is born, ה׳'s role in creating a person, and what decides a baby's gender
overview: This amud is full of אגדה about how a baby is formed and born. It opens with the פסוק for the oath a baby takes before birth, and רבי אלעזר's picture of a baby floating in the womb like a nut in water. A ברייתא then describes where the baby lies during each three months of pregnancy, and says that labor pains come from the baby turning over. That is why labor is harder with a girl, who must also turn her face. Next come teachings about marital relations during pregnancy, including the danger of the ninetieth day and אביי's answer, 'שומר פתאים ה׳'. The גמרא then teaches that every person has three partners: father, mother, and הקדוש ברוך הוא. It follows with several פסוקים that praise ה׳'s wonders in the womb, the story of the thorn that saved a traveler, and teachings that ה׳ is involved in conception. The amud ends with what decides whether a baby is a boy or a girl, and a question about the sons of אולם whose answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: What is the verse for the baby's oath?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the פסוק that shows a baby is given an oath before it is born.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the verse?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a source in the פסוקים for the idea, taught just before this, that a baby is made to swear an oath before birth. This short question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier discussion said the baby is made to swear to be a צדיק and not a רשע. Now the גמרא wants that idea anchored in a verse.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the verse? (a request for a source in תנ״ך)

phrases.english: What is the verse?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the search for a source for the oath discussed just before this section.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which פסוק teaches that a baby takes an oath before birth.

steps.title: The verse: You made me swear from my mother's womb
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers with the פסוק ממעי אמי אתה גוזי from תהלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: "From my mother's womb You are gozi."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק from תהלים in which דוד says that God was גוֹזִי to him from his mother's womb.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Plainly, גוֹזִי means "took me out" of the womb. The גמרא reads it as "You made me swear," so the verse becomes a hint to the oath given before birth.

keyTerms.meaning: Plainly "took me out"; read here as "made me swear"

steps.confusionAlert: Do not be thrown off by the plain meaning of גוֹזִי ("took me out"). The גמרא is reading the same word in a second way, as "made me swear."

phrases.english: "From my mother's womb You are gozi."
phrases.notes: תהלים 71:6. The whole point rests on reading גוזי as "made me swear."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source is the פסוק ממעי אמי אתה גוזי (תהלים 71:6).

steps.title: How do we know גוזי means swearing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we know that the word גוזי refers to taking an oath.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where can we tell that this word "gozi" is a term for swearing?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions its own proof. The plain meaning of גוזי is not "oath," so how can we read it that way? This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof from step 2 only works if גוזי can mean an oath. The גמרא asks for evidence that the word has that meaning somewhere else in תנ״ך.

keyTerms.meaning: From where can it be shown? How do we know this meaning?
A word that means swearing an oath

phrases.english: From where can we tell that this "gozi"
is a word for making someone swear?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי מַשְׁמַע דְּהַאי גּוֹזִי לִישָּׁנָא דְּאִשְׁתְּבוֹעֵי הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the reading of the key word in the verse from step 2.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Evidence that the word גוזי can mean an oath.

steps.title: Proof from "cut off your hair"
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the פסוק גזי נזרך והשליכי to show that this word is tied to vows.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: "Cut off your hair and cast it away."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by quoting a פסוק in ירמיהו that uses the same root word גזי together with נזרך, a word connected to the vow of a נזיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נזיר cuts off his hair at the end of his vow. Because גזי appears in a verse about the נזיר's vow, the word is linked to vows and oaths. That supports reading גוזי in תהלים as "made me swear."

keyTerms.meaning: Your hair, the hair grown under the vow of a נָזִיר

steps.whatToRemember: The baby's oath before birth is hinted at in ממעי אמי אתה גוזי. We know גוזי can mean an oath because the same word appears with the נזיר's vow in גזי נזרך.

phrases.english: As it is written: "Cut off your hair and cast it away."
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 7:29. נזרך hints at a נזיר's vow, so the word גזי goes along with vows.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 3 with a second פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: In ירמיהו, גזי appears with the vow of a נזיר, so the word is connected to vows and oaths.

steps.title: The baby in the womb is like a nut in water
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר compares a baby in the womb to a nut floating in a bowl of water that sinks to either side when pressed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אלעזר said: What is a baby in its mother's womb like? Like a nut floating in a bowl of water. If a person presses it with his finger, it sinks this way or that way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching from רבי אלעזר that gives a picture of how a baby sits inside the womb.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The baby is not fixed in place. Like a nut floating on water, it moves to one side or the other when something presses on it. The teaching describes the baby as floating and easily shifted.

phrases.english: And רבי אלעזר said:
What is a baby in its mother's womb like?
Like a nut placed in a bowl of water,
if a person puts his finger on it,
it sinks this way or that way.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר לְמָה וָלָד דּוֹמֶה בִּמְעֵי אִמּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new teaching about the baby in the womb.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A baby in the womb floats and moves to either side when pressed, like a nut in a bowl of water.

steps.title: Where the baby lives during each part of pregnancy
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the baby lives in the lower, middle and upper sections of the womb in each three months, then turns over at birth, which causes labor pains.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: In the first three months the baby lives in the lower section, in the middle three months in the middle section, and in the last three months in the upper section. When its time to come out arrives, it turns over and comes out, and this is what causes labor pains.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא describing where the baby is in the womb during each three months of pregnancy and what happens at birth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא splits pregnancy into three periods of three months, and the baby moves up one section in each. At birth it turns over to come out, and the ברייתא says that turning is what causes חבלי אשה, labor pains.

keyTerms.meaning: A section or chamber (of the womb)

steps.whyThisMatters: The idea that labor pains come from the baby turning over is the basis for the next step, which explains why pains are greater with a girl.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
In the first three months,
the baby lives in the lower section;
in the middle months, the baby lives in the middle section;
in the last months, the baby lives in the upper section.
And once its time to come out arrives,
it turns over and comes out,
and this is what causes "a woman's labor pains."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues describing the baby in the womb, now by stages of pregnancy.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The baby moves up through three sections of the womb over the three parts of pregnancy, and its turning over at birth causes labor pains.

steps.title: Why labor pains are greater for a girl
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the ברייתא's idea explains a known teaching that labor pains for a girl are greater than for a boy.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is what we learned: The labor pains for a girl are greater than for a boy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא links the ברייתא's point, that turning over causes labor pains, to an earlier teaching that labor is harder with a girl than with a boy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If labor pains come from the baby turning over, then a difference in pain between a girl and a boy must come from a difference in how they turn. The גמרא only makes the connection here; steps 9 and 10 explain the details.
steps.whatToRemember: Labor pains come from the baby turning over at birth, and this explains why pains are greater with a girl than with a boy. Step 10 explains the details.

phrases.english: And this explains what we learned:
The labor pains of a girl
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets and some leave it out. The meaning is the same.

phrases.english: are greater than those of a boy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ברייתא in step 6 to explain an earlier known teaching.
steps.raayaObject: The teaching that labor pains for a girl are greater than for a boy.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's statement that labor pains are caused by the baby turning over.

steps.title: A verse showing the baby starts in the lowest part of the womb
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר brings a פסוק from תהלים to support the idea that the baby first develops in the lower section of the womb.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: Which פסוק teaches this? "When I was made in secret, I was woven in the lowest parts of the earth." The פסוק does not say "I lived" there. It says "I was woven" there.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר gives a פסוק as a source for the ברייתא's teaching that the baby starts out in the lowest section of the womb.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק uses "רקמתי" (I was woven), not "דרתי" (I lived). The point is that the time the baby was being 'woven', its first stage of forming, happened in the 'lowest parts'. That matches the ברייתא, which says the baby is in the lower section during the first three months.

keyTerms.meaning: the lowest parts of the earth (here hinting at the lower part of the womb)

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar said:
What is the verse?
"When I was made in secret,
I was woven in the lowest parts of the earth."
phrases.notes: תהלים 139:15

phrases.english: It does not say "I lived" there,
but rather "I was woven" there.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a scriptural source for the ברייתא in step 6 about the baby starting in the lower section.
steps.raayaObject: The baby is in the lower section of the womb during its first stage of forming.
steps.raayaSupportSource: תהלים 139:15, which says "רקמתי" (I was woven) in the lowest parts, not "דרתי" (I lived).

steps.title: Why are labor pains greater for a girl?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the turning at birth is harder when the baby is a girl.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about the labor pains for a girl, that they are greater than those for a boy?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question: if every baby turns over at birth, why are the pains bigger for a girl? This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 tied labor pains to the baby turning over. But that raises a new question: why would turning hurt more with a girl than with a boy? The גמרא wants the exact difference.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? (asks why two cases are treated differently)
the labor pains of a girl

phrases.english: What is different about the labor pains of a girl,
that they are greater than those of a boy?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא חֶבְלֵי נְקֵבָה מְרוּבִּין מִשֶּׁל זָכָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the teaching mentioned in step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the turning at birth causes more pain for a girl than for a boy.

steps.title: A girl must turn her face around; a boy does not
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a boy is born facing the same way he lies in marital relations, and so is a girl. Because of this, a girl must turn her face before birth and a boy does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: This one (a boy) comes out the way he lies in marital relations, and that one (a girl) comes out the way she lies in marital relations. So she turns her face around, and he does not turn his face around.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: a girl turns her face during birth and a boy does not, so her birth involves more turning and more pain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A boy is born facing downward, the same as his position in marital relations. A girl is born facing upward, the same as her position. So the girl has to turn her face around before birth and the boy does not, and that extra turning causes extra pain.

keyTerms.meaning: in the manner of his/her marital relations (facing down for a male, up for a female)

phrases.english: This one (a boy) comes out the way he lies in marital relations,
phrases.notes: A boy faces downward, the way a man lies during relations.

phrases.english: and that one (a girl) comes out the way she lies in marital relations,
so this one (the girl) turns her face around,
and this one (the boy) does not turn his face around.

steps.whatToRemember: Labor pains come from the baby turning over. A girl must also turn her face to come out facing up, so her birth is harder.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A girl is born facing upward, so she must turn her face around. A boy is born facing downward and does not turn, so his birth is less painful.

steps.title: How marital relations affect mother and baby in each third of pregnancy
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says marital relations are hard on both mother and baby in the first three months, hard on the mother but good for the baby in the middle three months, and good for both in the last three months.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: In the first three months, marital relations are hard on the woman and also hard on the baby. In the middle three months, they are hard on the woman but good for the baby. In the last three months, they are good for the woman and good for the baby, because this way the baby comes out fair-skinned and strong.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about pregnancy, dividing it into three stages of three months each.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This fits the earlier idea that pregnancy has three stages of three months. The ברייתא gives a different result for each stage: first both are harmed, then only the mother, and finally both benefit. The reason given for the last stage is that the baby comes out healthy and strong.

keyTerms.meaning: the middle ones (the middle three months)

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
In the first three months of pregnancy:
marital relations are hard on the woman,
and also hard on the baby.
In the middle three months: hard on the woman
but good for the baby.
In the last three months: good for the woman
and good for the baby,
because as a result, the baby is found to be
fair-skinned and strong.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic that uses the same three-stage view of pregnancy from step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: First three months: harmful to mother and baby. Middle three: harmful to mother, good for baby. Last three: good for both, making the baby fair-skinned and strong.

steps.title: A warning about the ninetieth day
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that having marital relations on the ninetieth day of pregnancy is like spilling blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: One who has marital relations on the ninetieth day is as if he spills blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes another ברייתא with a strong warning about one specific day of pregnancy. This sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ninetieth day is the end of the first three months, the stage the earlier ברייתא called harmful for both. This ברייתא says that day is especially dangerous, so much so that it is compared to spilling blood.

phrases.english: It was taught: One who has marital relations on the ninetieth day,
phrases.notes: The ninetieth day of the pregnancy, the end of the first three months.

phrases.english: it is as if he spills blood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a sharper warning about one day at the end of the first three months.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Relations on the ninetieth day of pregnancy are as dangerous as spilling blood.

steps.title: How could anyone know it is the ninetieth day?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how a person could ever know exactly which day is the ninetieth day of pregnancy.
steps.simpleTranslation: How would he know?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא: the warning seems impossible to follow, because nobody knows the exact day the pregnancy began.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A rule about one exact day only helps if people can tell when that day is. Since the start of a pregnancy cannot be pinned down, the warning seems impossible to keep.

phrases.english: How would he know?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether the warning of step 12 can be followed at all.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's warning about the ninetieth day.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: No one can know when a pregnancy began, so no one can know which day is the ninetieth. The warning seems impossible to keep.

steps.title: אביי: go ahead, and ה׳ protects the simple
steps.stepSummary: אביי says a person may go ahead with marital relations as usual and rely on the פסוק "ה׳ protects the simple."
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, אביי said: He may go ahead and have relations, and "ה׳ protects the simple."
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the challenge: since no one can know the exact day, a person does not need to worry about it and may rely on ה׳'s protection.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי does not say the danger is gone. He says that when a person cannot possibly know about a danger, he may act normally and trust ה׳ to protect him. The פסוק "שומר פתאים ה׳" is the basis for this trust.

keyTerms.meaning: he goes ahead and has relations as usual
ה׳ protects the simple (people who cannot know about a danger)

phrases.english: Rather, Abaye said:
He may go ahead and have relations,
and "ה׳ protects the simple."
phrases.notes: תהלים 116:6

steps.whatToRemember: When a danger cannot be known, a person may act normally and rely on "שומר פתאים ה׳".
steps.whyThisMatters: The principle of "שומר פתאים ה׳" is used in other places in the גמרא too, for risks that people commonly take and cannot avoid.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical guidance: rely on ה׳'s protection for a danger that cannot be known.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the day cannot be known, it seemed the ברייתא's warning could not be followed and a person would be stuck.
steps.terutzMaskana: A person may go ahead as usual and rely on "שומר פתאים ה׳".

steps.title: Three partners in making a person
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a person has three partners: the father, the mother, and הקדוש ברוך הוא. It lists what each one contributes.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: A person has three partners: הקדוש ברוך הוא, his father, and his mother. The father gives the white seed, which forms the bones, sinews, nails, brain, and the white of the eye. The mother gives the red seed, which forms the skin, flesh, hair, and the black of the eye. ה׳ gives the spirit, the soul, the look of the face, sight, hearing, speech, walking, understanding, and wisdom.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא, continuing its discussion of how a baby forms. The ברייתא lists what each of the three partners puts into a person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The father's part is the hard and white parts of the body. The mother's part is the softer and darker parts. ה׳'s part is everything that makes the body alive and able to function: the soul, the senses, movement, and the mind.

keyTerms.meaning: white (here, the white seed of the father)
red (here, the red seed of the mother)
the look or features of the face

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the next step. Once we know which part is ה׳'s, we can understand what happens when He takes it back at death.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
There are three partners in a person:
The Holy One, Blessed be He, and his father, and his mother.
His father emits the white seed,
from which come the bones, the sinews, the nails,
the brain that is in his head, and the white of the eye.
His mother emits red seed,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁמִּמֶּנּוּ עוֹר, וּבָשָׂר, וּשְׂעָרוֹת, וְשָׁחוֹר שֶׁבָּעַיִן.
phrases.english: from which come the skin, the flesh, the hair, and the black of the eye.

phrases.aramaic: וְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא נוֹתֵן בּוֹ רוּחַ, וּנְשָׁמָה,
phrases.english: And the Holy One, Blessed be He, puts into him a spirit, a soul,
the features of the face, sight of the eye,
hearing of the ear, speech of the mouth,
walking of the legs, understanding, and wisdom.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: שְׁלֹשָׁה שׁוּתָּפִין יֵשׁ בָּאָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the laws of relations during pregnancy into a new אגדה about how a person is formed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person is made by three partners. The father and mother form the physical body, and ה׳ gives life, the senses, and the mind.

steps.title: At death, ה׳ takes back His part
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. When a person dies, ה׳ takes back His part and leaves the parents' part, the body, behind.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the time comes for a person to leave the world, ה׳ takes His part, and He leaves the father's and mother's part in front of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The same ברייתא continues and describes what happens when a person dies. ה׳ takes back what He gave, and only the body made by the parents is left.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This builds directly on the list in the last step. The soul, the senses, and the mind leave with ה׳. What stays behind is only the bones, flesh, and skin that the parents gave.

keyTerms.meaning: leaves it in front of them

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵיוָן שֶׁהִגִּיעַ זְמַנּוֹ לְהִפָּטֵר מִן הָעוֹלָם,
phrases.english: And when his time to depart from the world arrives,
the Holy One, Blessed be He, takes His part,
and the part of his father and mother, He leaves before them.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵיוָן שֶׁהִגִּיעַ זְמַנּוֹ לְהִפָּטֵר מִן הָעוֹלָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא, describing the end of the partnership at death.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: At death ה׳ takes back the life-giving part, and only the physical body from the parents remains.

steps.title: רב פפא's saying about salt and meat
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says this matches the popular saying: shake off the salt and throw the meat to the dog.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: This is what people mean when they say, "Shake off the salt, and throw the meat to the dog."
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא adds a popular saying that shows the point of the ברייתא. Without ה׳'s part, the body is worth nothing on its own, like meat without its salt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Salt is what keeps meat from spoiling. Once the salt is removed, the meat goes bad and is only good for a dog. In the same way, ה׳'s part is what keeps the body alive and valuable, and without it the body falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: this is what people say (a popular saying that fits the idea)

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
This is what people say:
"Shake off the salt,
phrases.notes: Salt keeps meat fresh. Without it the meat spoils.

phrases.english: and throw the meat to the dog."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the point of the ברייתא's last line with a popular saying.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Without ה׳'s part, the body is worthless, like meat after its salt is removed.

steps.title: The baby stays safe in an open womb
steps.stepSummary: רב חיננא בר פפא explains a פסוק in איוב. A person cannot be sure that an item in a tied-up flask with its opening up stays safe, but ה׳ keeps a baby safe in an open womb that faces down.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חיננא בר פפא explained the פסוק "He does great things beyond understanding, and wonders without number." Come and see how ה׳'s ways are unlike the ways of people. If a person puts something in a tied flask with its opening facing up, it may stay safe or it may not. But ה׳ forms a baby inside a woman's womb that is open and faces down, and the baby stays safe.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching begins. רב חיננא בר פפא explains a פסוק about ה׳'s wonders by comparing how people store things with how ה׳ keeps a baby in the womb.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person can do everything right, tie the flask and keep the opening up, and still not be sure nothing falls out. The womb is the opposite: it is open and faces down, yet the baby stays inside. This is one of the "wonders without number" in the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: the way of flesh and blood (human beings)
a tied-up flask or leather bottle

phrases.english: Rav Chinnana bar Pappa taught:
What is the meaning of what is written:
"Who does great deeds beyond understanding,
phrases.notes: איוב 9:10

phrases.english: and wonders without number"?
Come and see

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא כְּמִדַּת הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מִדַּת בָּשָׂר וָדָם.
phrases.english: that the way of flesh and blood is not like the way of the Holy One, Blessed be He.
The way of flesh and blood:
he puts an item into a tied flask
with its opening facing up,
and it is uncertain whether it stays safe or does not stay safe.
But the Holy One, Blessed be He,
forms the fetus inside a woman, in an open womb,
with its opening facing down, and it stays safe.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּרֵשׁ רַב חִינָּנָא בַּר פָּפָּא: מַאי דִכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new אגדה about the womb, using a פסוק to show ה׳'s wonders in forming a baby.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ה׳ keeps a baby safe in an open, downward-facing womb, something people cannot do even with a tied flask facing up.

steps.title: The heavier the baby, the higher it rises
steps.stepSummary: A second explanation of the פסוק: on a scale, heavier things go down, but a baby in the womb rises higher as it gets heavier.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation: A person puts his things on a scale, and the heavier they are, the lower they go. But with ה׳, the heavier the baby gets, the higher it rises.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second example of how ה׳'s ways are unlike human ways, explaining the same פסוק. The baby goes against the normal rule of weight.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally weight pulls things down, as anyone can see on a scale. A growing baby does the opposite and moves upward in the womb as it gets heavier. This is another "wonder" the פסוק is talking about.
steps.whatToRemember: A person has three partners: father, mother, and ה׳. ה׳'s part gives life, and without it the body is worthless. The womb shows ה׳'s wonders twice: the baby stays safe even though the womb is open and faces down, and the baby rises as it grows heavier.

phrases.english: Another explanation:
A person puts his items on the pan of a scale;
the heavier it gets, the lower it goes down.
But with the Holy One, Blessed be He,

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל זְמַן שֶׁמַּכְבִּיד הַוָּלָד עוֹלֶה לְמַעְלָה.
phrases.english: the heavier the baby gets, the higher it rises.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּבָר אַחֵר: אָדָם נוֹתֵן חֲפָצָיו לְכַף מֹאזְנַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, different example explaining the same פסוק from step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Unlike things on a scale, a baby rises in the womb as it grows heavier, which is another of ה׳'s wonders.

steps.title: Seeds in a garden versus a baby in the womb
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי הגלילי explains a פסוק in תהלים. When a person plants different seeds, each grows as its own kind, but in the womb ה׳ makes the seeds of both parents come out as one kind.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי הגלילי taught: What does the פסוק mean, 'I thank You, for I am wonderfully made; Your works are wonderful, and my soul knows it well'? Come and see how different people are from ה׳. When a person plants different seeds in one garden bed, each one comes up as its own kind. But when ה׳ forms a baby inside a woman, all the seeds come out as one kind.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי הגלילי explains a פסוק that praises how wonderfully ה׳ makes a person. He compares a human gardener to ה׳ forming a baby.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a garden, mixing different seeds still gives you separate plants. In the womb, the seeds of the father and the mother join and become one single baby. That is the 'wonder' the פסוק is praising.

keyTerms.meaning: The way of 'flesh and blood', meaning how human beings do things
A fetus, a baby still in the womb

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei HaGelili taught:
What is the meaning of what is written:
"I will thank You (Lord), for I am fearfully and wonderfully made;
phrases.notes: תהלים 139:14. Some versions have the word in round brackets and some don't.

phrases.english: wonderful are Your works, and my soul knows it very well"?
Come and see

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא כְּמִדַּת הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מִדַּת בָּשָׂר וָדָם.
phrases.english: that the way of flesh and blood is not like the way of the Holy One, Blessed be He.
The way of flesh and blood:
a person puts different seeds in one garden bed,
and each and every one comes up as its own kind.
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the words in round brackets; the words in square brackets are the corrected wording. Same meaning either way.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִילּוּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא צָר הָעוּבָּר בִּמְעֵי אִשָּׁה,
phrases.english: But the Holy One, Blessed be He, forms the fetus in a woman's womb,
and they all come out as one kind.
phrases.notes: "They all" means the seed of the father and of the mother; together they become one baby.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּרֵשׁ רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי מַאי דִכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the aggadic theme of ה׳'s wonders in forming a baby, now with a new פסוק and a new speaker.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Unlike seeds in a garden that each grow separately, the parents' seeds join in the womb to form one being.

steps.title: Dyes in a pot versus a baby in the womb
steps.stepSummary: A second explanation: when a dyer mixes dyes in one pot they all become one color, but in the womb each parent's seed keeps its own kind and forms its own parts of the baby.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation: a dyer puts different dyes into a pot, and they all come out as one color. But when ה׳ forms a baby in a woman, each seed comes out as its own kind.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, opposite comparison to show ה׳'s wonder from another angle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the human example is mixing, where everything blends together. In the womb, the father's seed and the mother's seed each make their own separate parts, as listed back in step 15. So ה׳ does the opposite of the dyer.

keyTerms.meaning: A large cooking pot or cauldron

steps.confusionAlert: The two explanations sound like they contradict each other (one kind vs. each its own kind). They are two different angles: the parents' seeds join to make one baby, yet each seed still builds its own parts of that baby.
steps.whatToRemember: ה׳'s work in the womb is wonderful both ways: the parents' seeds join into one person, yet each still forms its own separate parts.

phrases.english: Another explanation:
a dyer puts herbs into a cauldron,
and they all come out as one color.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִילּוּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא צָר הָעוּבָּר בִּמְעֵי אִשָּׁה,
phrases.english: But the Holy One, Blessed be He, forms the fetus in a woman's womb,
and each and every one comes out as its own kind.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second reading of the same פסוק from step 20, using an opposite comparison.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Unlike dyes that blend into one color, each parent's seed keeps its own kind and forms its own parts.

steps.title: Why thank ה׳ for being angry?
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף quotes a פסוק in ישעיהו that thanks ה׳ for being angry, and asks what situation the פסוק is describing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף taught: What does the פסוק mean, 'I thank You, ה׳, for You were angry with me; Your anger turns away and You comfort me'? What is the פסוק talking about?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף brings a puzzling פסוק and asks what it is talking about. He is setting up the story that answers it in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is strange to thank ה׳ for being angry with you. רב יוסף asks for a real-life case where a person would actually do that.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the פסוק talking about?

phrases.english: Rav Yosef taught:
What is the meaning of what is written:
"I will thank You, Lord, for You were angry with me;
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 12:1

phrases.english: Your anger turns away, and You comfort me"?
About what is the verse speaking?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new aggadic teaching on a different פסוק, linked to the theme of thanking ה׳.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What real situation would make someone thank ה׳ for His anger?

steps.title: The thorn that saved a traveler's life
steps.stepSummary: Two men set out on a business trip. One got a thorn stuck in him and cursed his bad luck. Later he heard his friend's ship sank, and he began to thank ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is talking about two people who set out on a business trip. One got a thorn stuck in him and started cursing. Days later he heard that his friend's ship had sunk at sea, and he started thanking and praising ה׳. That is why the פסוק says, 'Your anger turns away and You comfort me.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers his question with a story. What looked like ה׳'s anger, a painful thorn, turned out to save the man's life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The thorn kept him from getting on the ship, so it was really a hidden kindness. At first he cursed, but once he saw the full picture he thanked ה׳ for the very thing that hurt him. That is how a person can thank ה׳ 'for You were angry with me.'
steps.whatToRemember: Something that feels like a punishment from ה׳ may really be protecting us; later we may come to thank ה׳ for it.

phrases.english: About two people
who set out on a business trip.
A thorn got stuck in one of them,
and he started cursing and blaspheming.
Some days later he heard
that his friend's ship had sunk in the sea,
and he started thanking and praising.
That is why it says:
"Your anger turns away, and You comfort me."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22 with a story.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק describes someone whose suffering (a thorn) turned out to save his life, so he thanks ה׳ for that 'anger.'

steps.title: Even the one saved by a miracle does not see it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא links the thorn-and-ship story to רבי אלעזר's teaching that ה׳ alone knows the wonders He does, and that even the person saved does not recognize his own miracle.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what רבי אלעזר said: What does the פסוק mean, 'Who does wonders alone, and blessed is His glorious name forever'? Even the person a miracle happens to does not recognize his own miracle.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the story we just learned fits a teaching of רבי אלעזר: often only ה׳ knows that a miracle happened.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 23, the man cursed the thorn and only later understood that it saved him. רבי אלעזר reads 'לבדו' (alone) to mean that only ה׳ sees the miracle as it happens. The person himself does not recognize it. This ties the story to a פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is the same as. It connects what came before to another teaching.
Alone. Here it means only ה׳ knows.
The person the miracle happened to

steps.whatToRemember: Hidden miracles: a person may be saved without knowing it, and only ה׳ sees it.

phrases.english: And this is what Rabbi Elazar said:
What is the meaning of what is written:
"Who does (great) wonders alone,"
phrases.notes: תהלים 72:18. The word in round brackets is in the printed גמרא, but the corrected wording leaves it out.

phrases.english: "and blessed is His glorious name forever"?
Even the person the miracle happened to
does not recognize his own miracle.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ties the thorn-and-ship story to a teaching of רבי אלעזר on a פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only ה׳ knows the miracles He does. Even the person saved does not recognize his miracle.

steps.title: A person is formed only from the choice part of the drop
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא בר פפא reads 'זרית' in a פסוק in תהלים as 'winnowed.' He learns that a person is formed only from the clear, choice part of the drop.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא בר פפא taught: What does the פסוק mean, 'My going and my lying down You have winnowed, and You know all my ways'? It teaches that a person is not formed from the whole drop, only from its choice part.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the theme of how a baby is formed, with a new reading of a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word זֵרִיתָ can mean 'winnowed,' like separating grain from chaff. ארחי ורבעי are read as hints to intimacy. So the פסוק is read as saying that ה׳ picks out only the best part of the drop to form the person.

keyTerms.meaning: You have winnowed, meaning You separated the good from the waste
My going and my lying down. Here they are read as hints to intimacy.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina bar Pappa taught:
What is the meaning of what is written:
"My going and my lying down You have winnowed,"
phrases.notes: תהלים 139:3. He reads זֵרִיתָ as 'winnowed,' the way a farmer separates grain from chaff.

phrases.english: "and You are familiar with all my ways"?
This teaches that a person is not formed
from the whole drop,
but only from the choice part of it.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּרֵישׁ רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בַּר פָּפָּא מַאי דִכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from hidden miracles back to the wonders of forming a baby.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person is formed only from the choice part of the drop, which ה׳ 'winnows' out.

steps.title: Parable of the man winnowing grain
steps.stepSummary: דבי רבי ישמעאל gives a parable for the previous teaching: a man winnowing in the granary keeps the food and leaves the waste.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: It is like a man winnowing in the granary. He takes the food and leaves the waste.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a simple picture to explain רבי חנינא בר פפא's teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Winnowing separates grain from chaff. In the same way, ה׳ takes only the useful part of the drop to form a person and leaves the rest. The parable makes the meaning of זֵרִיתָ easy to picture.

keyTerms.meaning: Winnows, tosses grain so the chaff blows away

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
It is like a person
who winnows in the granary;
he takes the food
and leaves the waste.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל מָשָׁל לְאָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates step 25 with a parable.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Forming a person is like winnowing: the good part is kept and the waste is left behind.

steps.title: Two spellings of 'girded me' in דוד's song
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings רבי אבהו, who points out that דוד's song spells the same word without an א in שמואל and with an א in תהלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: This fits רבי אבהו's teaching. רבי אבהו pointed out a contradiction: One פסוק says 'ותזרני חיל' and another says 'האל המאזרני חיל.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up רבי אבהו's teaching by showing two different spellings of one word. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דוד's song appears twice, once in שמואל ב and once in תהלים. One spelling lacks an א, which looks like the root for 'winnow' (זרה). The other has an א, which means 'gird.' Why the difference?

keyTerms.meaning: Points out a contradiction (between two sources)
You girded me. It is spelled without an א, so it sounds like 'winnowed.'
Who girds me. It is spelled with an א.

phrases.english: This is like the teaching of Rabbi Abahu,
for Rabbi Abahu pointed out a contradiction:
It is written: "You girded me with strength,"
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 22:40. Spelled without an א.

phrases.english: and it is written: "The God Who girds me with strength."
phrases.notes: תהלים 18:33. Spelled with an א.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings another source that supports the 'winnowing' idea.
steps.kashyaTarget: The two spellings of the same word in דוד's song
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same song uses two different spellings, so each spelling must teach something.

steps.title: דוד: You winnowed me and You strengthened me
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו explains that דוד meant both things. ה׳ winnowed him, forming him from the choice part of the drop, and ה׳ also strengthened him.
steps.simpleTranslation: דוד said before הקדוש ברוך הוא: Master of the world, You winnowed me and You strengthened me.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו resolves the two spellings: each one teaches a different thing ה׳ did for דוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The spelling without an א hints to זֵירִיתַנִי, 'You winnowed me,' meaning ה׳ formed דוד from the choice part of the drop. The spelling with an א means 'You girded me,' meaning ה׳ gave him strength. This is why it supports רבי חנינא בר פפא.

keyTerms.meaning: You winnowed me, meaning You formed me from the choice part
You strengthened me, You made me energetic

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר דָּוִד לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא:
phrases.english: David said before the Holy One, Blessed be He:
Master of the world,
You winnowed me and You strengthened me.
phrases.notes: Each spelling from the last step hints to one of these two words.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר דָּוִד לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Both readings are true; each spelling teaches a different point.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two spellings seem to clash.
steps.terutzMaskana: One spelling means 'You winnowed me' and the other means 'You strengthened me.'

steps.title: ה׳ waits for the drop that will form a צדיק
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו reads 'רובע ישראל' in בלעם's blessing as teaching that ה׳ counts the times of intimacy of ישראל, waiting for the drop that will form a צדיק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו taught: What does the פסוק mean, 'Who has counted the dust of יעקב and numbered the רובע of ישראל'? It teaches that הקדוש ברוך הוא sits and counts the times of intimacy of ישראל, waiting for when the drop will come from which the צדיק will be formed.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו gives one more teaching about forming a person, this time from a פסוק in בלעם's blessing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word רוֹבַע is read as related to רְבִיעָה, a word for intimacy. So 'counting the רובע of ישראל' means ה׳ keeps track of these times. He is waiting for the moment a צדיק will be formed.

keyTerms.meaning: Here it is read as a hint to intimacy

steps.whatToRemember: This section shows ה׳'s close care in forming each person: He picks the choice part of the drop and waits for the צדיק to be formed.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abahu taught:
What is the meaning of what is written:
"Who has counted the dust of Jacob,"
phrases.notes: במדבר 23:10, from בלעם's blessing.

phrases.english: "and numbered the רובע of Israel"?
phrases.notes: He reads רוֹבַע as a hint to intimacy.

phrases.english: It teaches that the Holy One, Blessed be He, sits
and counts the times of intimacy of Israel,
waiting for when the drop will come
from which the righteous person will be formed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another teaching from רבי אבהו on the theme of forming a person.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ה׳ counts the times of intimacy of ישראל, waiting for the drop from which a צדיק will be formed.

steps.title: בלעם is blinded for mocking this idea
steps.stepSummary: Because of the idea that ה׳ counts the times of intimacy of ישראל, בלעם mocked it and was blinded at once.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because of this very matter, the eye of the wicked בלעם went blind. He said: Would the One who is pure and holy, whose servants are pure and holy, look at such a thing?! Right away his eye went blind, as the פסוק says: 'The words of the man whose eye is shut.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the teaching from step 29 and tells what happened when בלעם heard this idea. He mocked it and was punished with blindness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בלעם thought it was beneath a holy G-d to be involved in something as private as intimacy. The גמרא shows he was wrong, because ה׳ is involved there to bring a צדיק into the world. The proof that he was blinded is the פסוק calling him 'the man whose eye is shut.'

phrases.english: And because of this matter, the eye went blind
of the wicked Balaam.
He said: The One who is pure and holy,
and whose servants are pure and holy,
should He peek at such a thing?!
Immediately his eye went blind,
as it is written: "The saying of the man whose eye is shut."
phrases.notes: במדבר 24:3

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעַל דָּבָר זֶה נִסְמֵית עֵינוֹ שֶׁל בִּלְעָם הָרָשָׁע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי אבהו's teaching about 'רובע ישראל' and tells what happened to בלעם, who mocked it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בלעם mocked the idea that ה׳ is involved in intimacy and was blinded, as the פסוק 'שתום העין' shows.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: ה׳ helped in the conception of יששכר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says that רבי יוחנן taught the same idea: ה׳ helped in the night when יששכר was conceived, as hinted by 'יששכר חמור גרם.'
steps.simpleTranslation: This is the same as what רבי יוחנן said: What does the פסוק 'And he lay with her that night' mean? It teaches that ה׳ helped in that act, as it says: 'יששכר is a strong donkey.' A donkey caused יששכר to come about.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support from רבי יוחנן that ה׳ really is involved in the forming of a child. The example is the night יששכר was conceived.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'בלילה הוא' (that night) show something special was going on. The גמרא reads 'חמור גרם' as 'a donkey caused': ה׳ led יעקב's donkey to לאה's tent, so יששכר was conceived. This fits the earlier teaching that ה׳ is involved in this private act.

keyTerms.meaning: a strong-boned donkey (read here as 'a donkey caused')
יששכר, son of יעקב and לאה

phrases.english: And this is what Rabbi Yochanan said:
What is the meaning of what is written:
"And he lay with her that night"?
phrases.notes: בראשית 30:16, about יעקב and לאה.

phrases.english: It teaches that the Holy One, Blessed be He,
helped in that act,
as it is stated: "Issachar is a strong-boned donkey"
phrases.notes: בראשית 49:14

phrases.english: A donkey caused Issachar.
phrases.notes: The idea: ה׳ steered יעקב's donkey toward לאה's tent, so the donkey 'caused' יששכר to be born.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a matching teaching that supports the idea from steps 29-30 that ה׳ is involved in intimacy.
steps.raayaObject: The idea that ה׳ is involved in the act that forms a child.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's reading of 'בלילה הוא' together with 'יששכר חמור גרם.'

steps.title: What decides if the baby is a boy or a girl
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק quoting רבי אמי: if the woman emits seed first, the baby is a boy. If the man emits seed first, the baby is a girl. The source is a פסוק in ויקרא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said in the name of רבי אמי: If the woman emits seed first, she gives birth to a boy. If the man emits seed first, she gives birth to a girl. As it says: 'A woman, when she bears seed and gives birth to a male.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: what decides a baby's gender. רבי אמי gives a rule and a פסוק as the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק puts 'a woman bears seed' right next to 'gives birth to a male.' רבי אמי reads this as cause and effect: when the woman's seed comes first, the child is a boy. The opposite case, a girl, is understood from this.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק, אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said that Rabbi Ami said:
If the woman emits seed first,
she gives birth to a male.
If the man emits seed first,
she gives birth to a female,
as it is stated: "If a woman bears seed
and gives birth to a male."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 12:2

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק, אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from ה׳'s role in conception to a new question about what decides the baby's gender.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Woman first means a boy; man first means a girl, learned from 'אשה כי תזריע וילדה זכר.'

steps.title: רבי צדוק finds the source in the פסוק about לאה's children
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the gender rule was known long ago without a source, until רבי צדוק learned it from the פסוק about לאה's sons and דינה, יעקב's daughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: At first people would say that if the woman emits seed first she has a boy, and if the man emits seed first she has a girl. But the חכמים did not explain where this comes from, until רבי צדוק came and explained it: 'These are the sons of לאה whom she bore to יעקב in פדן ארם, and דינה his daughter.' The פסוק links the boys to the woman and the girl to the man.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא gives the same gender rule, but with a different source from a פסוק in בראשית. רבי צדוק was the first to explain it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פסוק, the boys are called 'sons of לאה,' linked to the mother. דינה is called 'his daughter,' linked to the father, יעקב. רבי צדוק reads this to mean that boys come when the woman's seed comes first, and girls when the man's seed comes first.

keyTerms.meaning: at first they used to say

steps.whatToRemember: Two sources for one rule: רבי אמי uses 'אשה כי תזריע וילדה זכר.' רבי צדוק uses 'בני לאה... ואת דינה בתו,' where the sons are linked to the mother and the daughter to the father.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the direction! Woman first means a boy, and man first means a girl. That is why the sons are called by לאה's name and דינה is called יעקב's daughter.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: At first they would say:
if the woman emits seed first, she gives birth to a male;
if the man emits seed first, she gives birth to a female.
But the Sages did not explain the matter,
phrases.notes: They didn't say which פסוק this rule comes from.

phrases.english: until Rabbi Tzadok came and explained it:
"These are the sons of Leah whom she bore to Jacob
in Paddan Aram, with Dinah his daughter."
phrases.notes: בראשית 46:15

phrases.english: It links the males to the female,
and the female to the male.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the same gender rule as step 32, but with a different source verse, from רבי צדוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The gender rule is learned from 'בני לאה... ואת דינה בתו': the sons are linked to the mother and the daughter to the father.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the rule was an old tradition. רבי צדוק gave it a source in the תורה, and that source is different from רבי אמי's.

steps.title: A second פסוק: the sons of אולם had many sons
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא brings a פסוק from דברי הימים about the sons of אולם, mighty archers who 'had many sons and grandsons,' as another hint to the rule about having boys.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And the sons of אולם were mighty men of valor, archers, and had many sons and grandsons."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new פסוק that will serve as another support for the rule taught in Step 32. It is only quoting the פסוק here; the explanation comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 33, רבי צדוק learned the rule from the פסוק about לאה's sons and דינה. Now a second פסוק is brought. The key words are 'had many sons,' and the next step asks why a person would get credit for that.

keyTerms.meaning: Archers (literally, men who step on the bow to string it)

phrases.english: "And the sons of Ulam were
phrases.notes: דברי הימים א ח:מ

phrases.english: mighty men of valor,
archers,
and had many sons and sons' sons."

steps.triggerLanguage: וַיִּהְיוּ בְנֵי אוּלָם אֲנָשִׁים גִּבּוֹרֵי חַיִל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second פסוק to the source given by רבי צדוק in Step 33.
steps.raayaObject: The rule from Step 32 that when the woman emits seed first the child is a boy, so a man's conduct can lead to having sons
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברי הימים א ח:מ, the sons of אולם who had many sons and grandsons

steps.title: Can a person control having many sons?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: is it really in a person's hands to have many sons and grandsons? It begins its answer with 'Rather, because...', and the rest of the answer continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it in a person's power to have many sons and grandsons? Rather, because...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a pointed question about the פסוק: children are a gift from Heaven, so why praise these men for having many sons? Then it starts to answer, setting up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question shows that the פסוק must mean something the men actually did. If having sons were completely out of their control, the פסוק would not mention it in their praise. This sets up the answer, which will tie the פסוק back to the rule from Step 32.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Is it then...?', which opens a question expecting the answer 'no'
In a person's hands, under his control
'Rather, because...', which opens the real explanation

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not doubting the פסוק. It is a way of showing that the פסוק must be hinting at something the men did themselves.

phrases.english: Is it in a person's hands
to have many sons and sons' sons?
Rather, because
phrases.notes: The sentence breaks off here; the answer finishes on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי בְּיָדוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם לְהַרְבּוֹת בָּנִים וּבְנֵי בָּנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks a question about the wording of the פסוק quoted in Step 34 in order to draw out its hidden lesson.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How can the פסוק credit people for having many sons, if that is not in a person's control?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The answer begins with 'אלא מתוך' and continues in the next part of the daf.
